claims.text: Section 299 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act says a person intending to construct or reconstruct a building must apply to the Commissioner with a site plan, ground plan, elevations, sections, work specification and other prescribed documents, prepared as required by rules/bye-laws.
claims.notes: Public transcription link; current bye-laws, category thresholds and prescribed checklist are not resolved.

claims.text: The current GBA public home lists Building Permission; BBMP's public citizen index lists approval jurisdiction, submission procedure, required documents, NOCs, fees, registered professionals, site inspection, Sakala and FAQ links.
claims.notes: Directory labels only; no live target was opened.

claims.text: The BPAS description says building plan approval is administered through town planning across eight BBMP zones and that an owner/applicant files online through a BBMP-registered architect, who creates the file and uploads the plan/documents.
claims.notes: Published 2019 IT description; current GBA/professional registration behavior is unknown.

claims.text: The BPAS description names a pre-DCR building plan in CAD format, applicable NOCs such as fire/water/pollution/environment, sale deed and Khata certificate as examples of uploads, with requirements depending on the proposal.
claims.notes: Examples are not a universal current checklist; no file was uploaded.

claims.text: The BPAS description says the inward clerk checks documents, an assistant engineer/case worker performs automated DCR scrutiny, gaps may be returned for correction, and an assistant engineer with ADTP conducts site inspection when documents are correct.
claims.notes: Dated workflow description; no scrutiny or inspection occurred.

claims.text: The BPAS description says license fee is calculated by built-up area, further approval routes through ADTP and larger general proposals involve chief engineer/joint commissioner, after which an online PDF license is generated/sent.
claims.notes: Fee amount, authority thresholds and current output timing are unknown.

claims.text: BBMP's public procedure page labels Sakala manual submission at sub-division office, Suvarna Paravanige and commencement/occupancy certificates at zonal office, and plan sanction at head office, alongside registered-professional links.
claims.notes: Public labels do not prove current eligibility or office routing for a supplied property.

claims.text: No reviewed official public source establishes a supplied property's approval jurisdiction, current building category/threshold, professional requirement, current document/NOC checklist, fee, sanction timing, inspection result or issued plan licence.
claims.notes: No architect login, property data, upload, payment, plan submission or case lookup.

roadblocks.title: Zone/category and GBA transition
roadblocks.symptom: Public pages list multiple routes (Sakala, Suvarna Paravanige, general/head office) while current GBA corporation/zone mapping is not shown.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Property location, proposal size/height/use and city-corporation transition.
roadblocks.recovery: Confirm current zone, category and competent authority before appointing/submitting through a professional.

roadblocks.title: Case-specific plans/NOCs/fees
roadblocks.symptom: Published examples do not establish the current checklist, NOC set, fee or professional registration for a supplied property.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Land use, proposal size/height, zoning, construction type and external clearances drive requirements.
roadblocks.recovery: Get the current category checklist and fee from Town Planning/registered professional; no upload or payment in this pass.

roadblocks.title: Scrutiny, inspection and sanction unobserved
roadblocks.symptom: No project number, scrutiny remark, inspection, demand, payment or licence exists.
roadblocks.likelyCause: These states require a real architect-led application and municipal processing.
roadblocks.recovery: Retain project/reference number after an authorised filing; displayed/dated workflows are not approval guarantees.
